analysis.title: The Speculative Grade Beat: Bonds Are Back
key_insights: Citi switches its asset allocation framework to a 55%/45% weighting in favor of high yield bonds over leveraged loans, reversing its late-June pivot to loans. The stated drivers are improving relative value, a steadier rates backdrop and rebounding high-beta performance.

Since the late-June pivot, the Morningstar/LSTA Leveraged Loan Index outperformed the Bloomberg High Yield Index by 253bp (+1.45% vs -1.08%), as rate pressure and high-beta underperformance (CCCs, AI) weighed on bonds.

The Treasury curve generally moved higher by 50-60bp over the period, led by the 5y yield, which rose 58bp. Credit spreads widened at the same time, led by high-beta segments, so the rate rise did not reflect a risk-on environment.
The Bloomberg Caa Index fell 5.51% and Citi's high yield AI basket fell 10.58% over the period. The Ba and B indices each lost less than 1%.

The loan market's carry advantage over bonds was 54bp in late June and is now gone. The yield on the High Yield BB/B Index equals the yield on the Non-Distressed Loan Tracker (using current 1mo/3mo SOFR) for the first time since early 2023.

Citi sees the rate backdrop as improved. The Fed's hold at Wednesday's meeting gives comfort that any rate increases will be measured, and Chairman Warsh said the goal 'isn't to throw sand in the gears of the economy'.

Citi expects the Treasury's quarterly refunding next Wednesday to pose more downside risk than upside risk to yields, and points to Secretary Bessent's 'asymmetric information' and 'house' comments from September.

On AI issuers, hyperscalers in particular are showing more sensitivity to tighter financial conditions. They are pursuing equity raises and giving more guidance on borrowing plans than they historically have, which is reassuring investors worried about mounting new issue debt totals.
Recent high yield new issues that had been sitting on significant losses have rebounded, which Citi cites as another encouraging sign for high-beta exposure.

sector_views.sector: High yield bonds vs leveraged loans
sector_views.rationale: Citi moves to a 55% high yield bond / 45% loan allocation because the loan carry advantage has closed, the rate backdrop has steadied and high-beta credit is rebounding.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Treasury selloff closed the carry advantage loans had over bonds, and rose alongside wider credit spreads rather than on risk-on sentiment.
Citi reads the hold, and Chairman Warsh's comments, as a sign that any rate increases will be measured.

trade_ideas.description: Shift the 55%/45% asset allocation framework from leveraged loans to high yield bonds
trade_ideas.rationale: The loan carry advantage (54bp in late June) is gone, the rate backdrop is steadier, and high-beta credit is rebounding.

risk_factors: Rate increases remain possible, though Citi expects them to be measured.
Treasury quarterly refunding next Wednesday could move yields, though Citi sees more downside than upside risk.
Mounting new issue debt totals from AI issuers have worried investors.
Financial conditions tightening could hit hyperscalers' issuance.

tension_points.bull_case: The loan carry advantage is gone, the rate backdrop is steadier, hyperscalers are more disciplined on borrowing, and recent high yield new issues have rebounded.
tension_points.bear_case: Rates rose 50-60bp alongside wider credit spreads, and Caa bonds and AI credits fell sharply, so high-beta exposure has been hurt.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Citi's refunding view, that Treasury refunding poses more downside than upside risk to yields, would be wrong if refunding pushes yields higher.
